claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 18 and lives at home with me. I wanted to check if I can still claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 18, his eligibility depends on whether he's in approved education or training. Children aged 16-19 can qualify for Child Benefit if they're staying in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in sixth form, college, studying A-levels, doing a traineeship, or similar approved education or training?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is! He's studying for his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you! Since Alex is studying for his A-levels, he would generally qualify under the education criteria for Child Benefit (children under 20 in approved education or training are eligible).

Let me ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex working, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment - he's just focusing on his studies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. A few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you here in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And yes, Alex lives here at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Are you the person who is responsible for Alex - meaning you're providing for his upkeep, food, clothes, etc.?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's actually a bit complicated. His other parent and I are both responsible for him, but we can't agree on who should claim the Child Benefit. We're both looking after him in different ways.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - that can be a tricky situation. Let me clarify a bit more:

Since you mentioned Alex lives at home with you in Manchester, does he live with you full-time, or does he split his time between you and his other parent?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with me full-time here in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful information.

Just to complete my assessment, let me ask:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, is his other parent already receiving Child Benefit payments for him?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is currently claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**Are you claiming any benefits yourself, and do you have any immigration status considerations?** (For example, do you have UK citizenship, settled status, pre-settled status, or any other immigration status I should be aware of?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure why you're asking about my immigration status or benefits - I thought this was just about whether Alex qualifies? I live in the UK and I'm asking about Child Benefit for my son who's doing his A-levels. Is there something specific you need to know?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're absolutely right, and I apologize for any confusion. I was just making sure I covered all the eligibility criteria, but I have enough information now to assess your situation.

Let me summarize what you've told me:

- Alex is 18 years old
- He lives with you full-time in Manchester, UK
- He's studying for his A-levels (approved education)
- He's not working
- You're responsible for him and he lives with you
- Nobody else is currently claiming Child Benefit for him

Based on the rules, since only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, and you and Alex's other parent disagree about who should claim, HMRC (HM Revenue and Customs) has a process to help resolve this. The rules state that if two people are responsible for the same child and cannot agree on who will get Child Benefit, HMRC will decide who will get it.

**Just to be clear: have you or Alex's other parent contacted HMRC about this disagreement, or would this be the first claim being made for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This would be the first claim being made for Alex. We haven't contacted HMRC about it yet - that's why I'm here trying to figure out if I'm even eligible to claim in the first place.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 18 and studying for his A-levels (which is approved education)
- He lives with you full-time in the UK
- He's not working 24 hours or more per week
- You're responsible for him
- No one is currently claiming Child Benefit for him

The key point is that under the rules, you would normally qualify for Child Benefit since you're responsible for Alex, he's under 20, he's in approved education, and he lives with you in the UK.

However, regarding the disagreement with Alex's other parent: the rules state that two people cannot get Child Benefit for the same child, and if you cannot agree between yourselves who will claim it, you should agree together or HMRC will decide. But since no one has claimed yet and Alex lives with you full-time, you would be eligible to make a claim.

Let me provide you with my formal assessment now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Assessment Complete

**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 18 and studying for his A-levels, which counts as approved education
- Child Benefit continues for children under 20 who are in approved education or training
- Alex lives with you full-time in the UK
- He's not working 24 hours or more per week
- You're responsible for him
- No one is currently claiming Child Benefit for him

Regarding the disagreement with Alex's other parent: since Alex lives with you full-time and you're his primary caregiver, you are eligible to make the claim. Only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child. If both of you were to claim, HMRC would decide, but typically it goes to the parent the child lives with.

You can now proceed to make a claim for Child Benefit. If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you should be aware of the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, which you may need to pay back through your tax return.
